text: My husband just informed me that he's had a very long, hard week at work, and so he just wants to enjoy the weekend in a clean house with some delicious home-cooked meals. And I said, that's great, because I know that his mother is going to love having him for a few days. So the guy says he's had a long week, wants to relax, enjoy a clean house and some home-cooked meals, and her answer is, that's great, your mom will love having you for a few days. Look, I'm not saying a woman has to cook or clean just because she's a woman. Relationships don't work that way anymore. It depends on your dynamic, who works more, and what you both agree on. But one thing that should always exist in a healthy relationship is empathy. If your partner worked hard all week and wants to recharge, and your first reaction is indifference instead of understanding, that's not partnership. And it goes both ways. If she's tired and he doesn't care, that's just as bad. In today's world, both partners might be working, both might be tired. Then order some food, skip the chores, and enjoy the weekend together. The point is to be on the same team. If your woman can't feel your exhaustion and doesn't want to make life a little easier for you when you are down, she is not your teammate. Find someone who is happy when you are at peace, who takes pride in making you feel good. That's what good relationship looks like.
